title: MARS: Dynamic Routing of Reinforcement-Learned Atomic Skills for Multi-Stage Robotic Manipulation
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong capabilities in multi-task robotic manipulation. However, they still face limitations in control precision and execution stability during critical manipulation stages, such as object grasping, alignment and insertion. To combine general-purpose manipulation capabilities with task-specific fine-grained control, while enabling effective coordination between generalist and specialized policies throughout multi-stage manipulation tasks, this paper proposes MARS (Modular Atomic-skill Routing System), a dynamic routing framework for reinforcement learning-based atomic skills. MARS integrates a frozen generalist VLA policy with multiple independently trained atomic skill policies. Using a shared RL Token state representation and the reference action of VLA, specialized control policies are optimized through reinforcement learning for different cr`itical manipulation stages. For high-level policy selection, we develop a dynamic router that integrates temporal context and skill semantics. The router employs Mamba-based recurrent encoding and a historical feature window to capture state evolution during manipulation. Skill descriptions of candidate policies are encoded into semantic queries, and attention mechanisms are used to establish correspondences between skill semantics and temporal state features. Experimental results show that MARS achieves an average Macro-F1 score of 90.47% across four LIBERO task suites under fixed-trajectory evaluation, outperforming an MLP-based router by 7.08 percentage points. In the simulated Tube Transport task, the full-task success rate increases from 20.04% to 85.67%. These results demonstrate that stage-specific reinforcement learning and temporal state-aware dynamic policy routing can improve multi-policy coordination and overall task execution performance in multi-stage robotic manipulation.

AI.tldr: MARS 冻结通用 VLA 策略，外挂多个独立训练的强化学习原子技能策略，并用 Mamba 时序编码＋技能语义注意力动态选择技能。作者报告：四个 LIBERO 任务套件平均 Macro-F1 90.47%，比 MLP 路由器高 7.08 个百分点；仿真 Tube Transport 全任务成功率从 20.04% 提升到 85.67%。
AI.motivation: VLA 模型已具备较强的多任务操作能力，但在抓取、对齐、插入等关键操作阶段的控制精度与执行稳定性仍不足。作者希望把通用操作能力与任务专用的细粒度控制结合，并在多阶段任务中让通用策略与专用策略有效协同。
AI.method: 输入是操作任务的多阶段流程；方法保留一个冻结的通用 VLA 策略，另训练多个针对不同关键阶段的原子技能策略（各自独立训练，通过强化学习优化）。技能策略使用共享的 RL Token 状态表示以及 VLA 的参考动作作为条件。高层选择由一个动态路由器完成：用 Mamba 循环编码加历史特征窗口捕捉状态演化，把候选策略的技能描述编码成语义查询，再用注意力在技能语义与时序状态特征之间建立对应关系。输出是当前阶段应执行哪个策略的决策，从而在多阶段任务中协调通用策略与专用策略。
AI.result: 作者报告两项结果：(1) 固定轨迹评测下，四个 LIBERO 任务套件平均 Macro-F1 为 90.47%，比 MLP 路由器高 7.08 个百分点；(2) 在仿真 Tube Transport 任务中，全任务成功率由 20.04% 提升到 85.67%。摘要未给出其他基线、方差、样本量或统计显著性。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能而言，该结果支持“阶段专用强化学习策略 + 时序状态感知的动态路由”可以改善多策略协调与多阶段操作的整体执行性能。但证据边界明确：定量结果只在 LIBERO 与仿真 Tube Transport 上报告，摘要未报告真实机器人实验、未报告路由延迟或推理开销，也未提供除 MLP 路由器之外的消融，因此不能推断真实部署效果或方法各组件各自的贡献。
AI.core_method: 冻结的通用 VLA 策略与多个 RL 训练的原子技能策略并行存在，由一个基于 Mamba 时序编码和技能语义注意力的路由器按阶段动态选择技能。

title: Self-Calibrating Vision-Agent-Action: Deploying Pick-and-Place to New Robot Cells without Demonstrations or Fine-Tuning
comment: 7 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables; supplementary video in ancillary files
summary: In simulation, Vision-Agent-Action (VAA) performs pick-and-place in robot cells with gripper or base-frame changes without robot demonstrations or fine-tuning. It uses pre-trained vision-language and language models for interpretation, measures the command map and camera geometry from its own motion and fingertips, estimates lens distortion, and plans grasps from measured object depth. A controlled study of eight public LIBERO-fine-tuned vision-language-action models (VLAs) varies robot hardware, camera geometry, appearance, and base frame. Gripper and frame changes dominate their losses in the tested fractional design. Across 18 cells with these changes, frozen VAA achieves 230/360 successes (64%), the refined VAA 268/360 (74%), and the strongest released VLA on this subset 76/360 (21%). Paired ablations support the self-calibration bundle, lens estimation under compounded changes, and the measured-depth pipeline. On a two-step LIBERO-Goal chain with object state carried between instructions, VAA completes 54/60 chains in changed cells, while four evaluated VLAs complete none.

AI.tldr: VAA 用自标定替代演示与微调，把 pick-and-place 迁移到改动过的仿真机器人单元；在 18 个改动单元中冻结版达 64%（230/360）、精化版 74%（268/360），最强已发布 VLA 仅 21%（76/360）。
AI.motivation: 机器人单元一旦更换夹爪、相机几何、外观或基座坐标系，已微调的 VLA 性能会明显下降；而按常规做法适配新单元需要机器人演示或微调。作者用一个八模型受控研究定位到：夹爪与坐标系变化是这些损失的主要来源。
AI.method: 输入是语言指令与相机观测。方法不改动预训练模型权重：用预训练视觉语言模型与语言模型做指令与场景解释，靠机器人自身的运动与指尖接触来测量指令映射和相机几何，估计镜头畸变，并用测量得到的物体深度来规划抓取，从而在新单元中输出 pick-and-place 动作，无需机器人演示或微调。相对基线的关键变化是把标定量从人工设定/学习权重改为自测。
AI.result: 在 18 个含夹爪与坐标系变化的仿真单元中，冻结 VAA 230/360（64%）、精化 VAA 268/360（74%）、该子集上最强已发布 VLA 76/360（21%）。两步 LIBERO-Goal 链（指令间传递物体状态）在改动单元中 VAA 完成 54/60，四个被评测 VLA 完成 0。八模型受控研究显示夹爪与坐标系变化主导其损失，但摘要未给出具体数值。配对消融支持自标定组合、复合变化下的镜头估计与实测深度流程，摘要同样未报告数值。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的意义是：自标定可作为一条不依赖演示与微调、面向新机器人单元的可迁移路径，且摘要证据指出硬件与坐标系变化比外观变化更关键。但全部结果均为作者报告的仿真结果（robot cells、LIBERO），摘要未报告真实机器人验证、开销或统计细节，因此不能外推为实机部署能力。
AI.core_method: 用预训练视觉语言与语言模型做解释，再通过机器人自身运动与指尖接触自测指令映射、相机几何与镜头畸变，并用实测深度规划抓取。

key_results.setting: 仿真 pick-and-place；18 个改动单元，变化涵盖机器人硬件、相机几何、外观与基座坐标系；对比对象为该子集上最强的已发布 VLA。摘要未报告随机种子、试验次数外的统计细节。
key_results.evidence_quote: Across 18 cells with these changes, frozen VAA achieves 230/360 successes (64%), the refined VAA 268/360 (74%), and the strongest released VLA on this subset 76/360 (21%).

key_results.finding: 在指令间传递物体状态的两步 LIBERO-Goal 链上，VAA 在改动后的单元中完成 54/60 条链，四个被评测 VLA 一条也未完成。

key_results.evidence_quote: On a two-step LIBERO-Goal chain with object state carried between instructions, VAA completes 54/60 chains in changed cells, while four evaluated VLAs complete none.

title: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
summary: Robots in homes, warehouses and farms must pick up objects they have never seen, usually without a 3D model or a category label. A grasping policy that works directly on the point cloud from a depth sensor needs only the geometry the robot observes, so it applies to any new object. Offline grasp generators such as Contact-GraspNet work this way, but they rank grasps by learned plausibility rather than by whether the grasp actually lifts the object. Reinforcement learning (RL) can optimize for that directly and make a point-cloud grasping policy much better on average, yet it leaves specific grasps persistently unsolved. We present a human-in-the-loop failure loop that targets those grasps: situations an RL policy keeps failing are mined automatically, sent to a virtual-reality application where a person picks the object up with their own hands, and returned to training as two grasp points. The person contributes only where to grasp; the robot chooses its own approach. In simulation, RL raises success on unseen objects from 55% with Contact-GraspNet to 83%. Adding 58 human demonstrations nearly doubles success on the hard cases RL kept failing, from 24% to 45%, and recovers performance that RL alone loses on similar cases that were never demonstrated, without reducing success on unseen objects.

AI.tldr: 强化学习能提升点云抓取策略的平均成功率，但会留下持续失败的具体抓取；本文用自动挖掘失败情形＋VR 人类示教（仅提供两个抓取点）回灌训练，在仿真中把难例成功率从 24% 提升到 45%，且不降低未见物体上的成功率。
AI.motivation: 家用、仓储和农业场景中的机器人需要抓取从未见过的物体，通常没有 3D 模型也没有类别标签；只依赖深度传感器点云几何的抓取策略可适用于任意新物体。但 Contact-GraspNet 这类离线抓取生成器按学到的"合理性"排序，而不是按抓取是否真能把物体抬起来排序；RL 虽能直接优化"抬起"这一目标并显著提升平均表现，却仍会留下特定的、持续失败的抓取。
AI.method: 输入：深度传感器获取的点云，以及一个基于 RL 训练的点云抓取策略。机制：自动挖掘该 RL 策略反复失败的抓取情形，把这些情形送入一个 VR 应用，由人在虚拟现实中用自己的手把物体拿起，该人工操作被转换为两个抓取点并回灌到训练中形成"人在回路"的失败修复闭环。人只贡献"抓哪里"，机器人的接近路径由策略自行决定。输出：经过示教数据再训练的抓取策略。相对基线的改变在于，不是替换 Contact-GraspNet 式排序或重做 RL 奖励，而是在 RL 已训练好的策略上，针对其持续失败的局部区域追加人类提供的抓取点监督。
AI.result: 作者报告：仿真中 RL 把未见物体上的成功率从 Contact-GraspNet 的 55% 提升到 83%；再加入 58 条人类示教后，RL 持续失败的难例成功率从 24% 提升到 45%（作者表述为"近乎翻倍"），并恢复了 RL 单独在未被示教的相似情形上丢失的性能，同时没有降低未见物体上的成功率。摘要未报告真实机器人实验、统计显著性或其他基线的数值。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的启示是：在点云抓取这类几何驱动任务中，纯 RL 的平均提升可能掩盖一批稳定的失败模式，而少量针对这些模式的人类示教（只标注抓取点，不标注接近轨迹）可以定向修补它们，并似乎能迁移到未被示教的相似情形。证据边界：所有数值均来自仿真，摘要未报告真实机器人验证、示教采集成本、失败挖掘的具体判据，因此"恢复性能"与"不降低未见物体成功率"均属作者在仿真条件下的自报结论，未经独立验证。
AI.core_method: 自动挖掘 RL 策略持续失败的抓取情形，让人类在 VR 中用手完成抓取，只把结果转成两个抓取点加回训练集。

key_results.finding: 仿真中，RL 将未见物体上的抓取成功率从 Contact-GraspNet 的 55% 提升到 83%。
key_results.setting: 点云抓取策略，未见物体（unseen objects），仿真实验；对比基线为离线抓取生成器 Contact-GraspNet；摘要未报告真实机器人条件。
key_results.evidence_quote: In simulation, RL raises success on unseen objects from 55% with Contact-GraspNet to 83%.

key_results.finding: 在 RL 持续失败的难例上，加入 58 条人类示教后成功率从 24% 提升到 45%，作者表述为近乎翻倍。
key_results.setting: RL 反复失败并被自动挖掘出的难例；示教数量 58 条；仿真条件；摘要未报告失败挖掘阈值与统计显著性。
key_results.evidence_quote: Adding 58 human demonstrations nearly doubles success on the hard cases RL kept failing, from 24% to 45%

key_results.finding: 示教还恢复了 RL 单独在未被示教的相似情形上丢失的性能，且未降低未见物体上的成功率。
key_results.setting: 与示教情形相似但从未被示教的情形，以及未见物体；仿真条件；摘要未给出对应数值或对照组细节。
key_results.evidence_quote: and recovers performance that RL alone loses on similar cases that were never demonstrated, without reducing success on unseen objects.

limitations: 摘要只报告仿真结果，未报告真实机器人实验（真实场景迁移是否成立，摘要未报告）。
摘要未报告失败挖掘的具体判据、示教采集时长或人力成本，也未报告统计显著性与重复次数。
摘要未报告与 Contact-GraspNet 之外其他基线的比较，也未报告 RL 策略本身的训练设置与硬件条件。

title: RoboCoEvo: Expanding Robot Capabilities through Agent-Policy Co-Evolution
summary: Integrating MLLM-based agents with robotic foundation models has attracted increasing attention as a means of enhancing robotic capabilities. However, the improvement of such integrated systems remains largely decoupled across their agent and model components, with advances in one component not necessarily benefiting the other, substantially limiting the capabilities of the combined system. As both MLLMs and robotic foundation models become increasingly capable, fully realizing their combined potential calls for co-evolution, an iterative process in which improvements in agents and robotic foundation models reinforce one another. We propose RoboCoEvo, a failure-guided co-evolution framework that couples the refinement of the agent's explicit and reusable executable knowledge with parameter learning in robotic foundation models, such as vision-language-action (VLA) models. Through a code-as-policy formulation, the agent develops and refines executable failure-detection and recovery programs, generating targeted corrective experience. Post-training consolidates the resulting corrective behaviors into the robotic model's end-to-end policy, improving autonomous task execution. Changes in the updated policy's failure distribution, in turn, guide subsequent revisions to the agent's programs. Experiments on BEHAVIOR-1K, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin demonstrate sustained improvements in autonomous VLA task performance across successive co-evolution rounds.

AI.tldr: 针对 MLLM 智能体与机器人基础模型“各自改进、互不增益”的解耦问题，作者提出 RoboCoEvo：用失败引导的智能体—策略协同进化，把智能体写出的失败检测/恢复程序转化为纠正经验，再后训练进 VLA 端到端策略，策略失败分布反过来指导智能体程序修改。摘要称在 BEHAVIOR-1K、RoboCasa、RoboTwin 上多轮协同进化中自主 VLA 任务性能持续提升，但未给出任何数值。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，将 MLLM 智能体与机器人基础模型集成虽受关注，但这类集成系统的提升基本是解耦的：一个组件的进步不一定让另一个组件受益，从而显著限制了组合系统的能力上限。作者认为在两者都越来越强的情况下，要兑现组合潜力需要“协同进化”，而非单侧改进。
AI.method: 输入是一个 MLLM 智能体加一个机器人基础模型（如 VLA 模型）构成的集成系统。做法是失败引导的迭代闭环：（1）以 code-as-policy 形式，让智能体开发并细化可复用的可执行知识——即失败检测与恢复程序，从而产生针对性的纠正经验；（2）通过后训练把这些纠正行为固化进机器人模型的端到端策略，改善自主任务执行；（3）已更新策略的失败分布发生变化，再用它指导下一轮智能体程序的修订。与原先“智能体与模型各自改进”的基线相比，变化点在于把双方的学习目标通过失败信号互相耦合。输出是一个随轮次迭代更新的智能体程序集合与更新后的机器人策略。
AI.result: 摘要只给出定性结论：在 BEHAVIOR-1K、RoboCasa、RoboTwin 上，随协同进化轮次推进，自主 VLA 任务性能持续提升。摘要未报告任何具体指标名称、数值、单位、提升幅度或对比基线，因此这属于作者自述结论，未经独立验证。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的意义在于提出了一种把 MLLM 智能体的显式可执行知识与 VLA 参数学习互相驱动的迭代范式，试图用失败信号打通“智能体—策略”的解耦瓶颈，并给出多轮迭代可持续改进的定性证据。证据边界：摘要只描述方法框架与三项基准上的定性趋势，未给出数值结果、对照方法、轮次数、真机与仿真的区分，因此无法判断提升幅度、统计可靠性或实际部署可行性。
AI.core_method: 让 MLLM 智能体用 code-as-policy 写出失败检测与恢复程序，将纠正经验后训练进 VLA 策略，再用新策略的失败分布反过来修订智能体程序，形成失败引导的迭代闭环。

title: Ego2Sim2Humanoid: Agentic Real-to-Sim for Learning Loco-Manipulation VLAs without Robot Demonstrations
summary: Imitation learning for visuomotor policies typically relies on teleoperated robot demonstrations, which are costly because every episode requires a trained operator controlling a physical robot in real time through teleoperation interfaces and wearable body-tracking hardware. Egocentric glasses capture human demonstrations without a robot or handheld grippers, yet they track only the head and in-view human hands, and directly copying human motion to a robot with different stature, arm reach and hand morphology fails to produce feasible contacts. \method{} converts egocentric glasses recordings into physically verified robot training trajectories. An agentic real-to-sim stage reconstructs collision and textured visual assets from the recorded RGB-D and head streams, completes unseen surfaces when needed, and predicts target contact bands on the manipulated objects. During motion adaptation, a grasp planner turns each contact band into a feasible robot wrist pose and finger closure, bilevel stance optimization plans collision-free standing postures that keep hand targets reachable, and a whole-body motion generator synthesizes lower-body locomotion and out-of-view arm motion. Two-stage motion correction then blends visibility transitions kinematically and trains a reinforcement-learning tracking policy in physics simulation under agent-designed semantic rewards, completing manipulation phases even when the object leaves the camera view. Rendering the reconstructed scene through the robot's onboard camera along the optimized rollout yields synchronized robot-view images, proprioception and verified action labels. title: Leaning Over to Reach Far-Away Objects
comment: 8 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Under review at ICRA 2027. Videos and code at this https URL
summary: We study supported reaching to extend a humanoid robot's workspace by bracing against the environment for stabilization using a straightforward yet capable whole-body model predictive control (MPC) approach, exclusively with local sensing and fiducial markers. While typical solutions for whole body humanoid control aim at avoiding or accommodating contact, contact is explicitly required to reach objects placed on surfaces far out of normal reach. We employ sampling-based MPC for whole-body leaning, bracing, reaching, and recovery on a Unitree H1-2 humanoid. The controller runs in real-time at 34 Hz on a laptop, transfers sim-to-real, extends reach by about 50 cm beyond the unbraced standing workspace, and sustains the loaded posture for over four minutes, before pose estimation drifts. The controller reaches the commanded target in 89% of trials and completes the full reach-and-recovery cycle in 81%, across 54 trials spanning six targets and three table heights. We further characterize why such a small real-time sampling budget is sufficient, finding that temporal persistence of sampled actions and exploration scale strongly govern success, while CEM provides the widest operating region over planning rate and model mismatch. These results establish a real-world baseline for online, contact-rich humanoid manipulation. Code, videos, and full hardware details are available at this https URL

title: VLN-Flash: Parallel Action Decoding with Adaptive Execution for Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: When a vision-and-language navigation policy generates an action sequence autoregressively, the robot waits for a chain of dependent predictions. A small discrete action vocabulary makes it possible to score all short-horizon plans in parallel. We introduce VLN-Flash, a training-free decoder that evaluates the complete action-prefix tree in a single forward pass. Branch-specific attention and matched token positions preserve the original policy's conditional action distribution for each prefix in exact arithmetic. We use the score margin between the stepwise-greedy prefix and its strongest alternative at each depth to decide how many actions to execute. The robot then executes the plan with the highest joint score at the chosen depth before observing again. On matched inputs, VLN-Flash achieves a nearly $3\times$ speedup in action decoding over native autoregression on Uni-NaVid and StreamVLN. Compared with the native autoregressive decoders, it improves success rate and success weighted by path length (SPL) on R2R-CE and RxR-CE, with success gains up to 2.7 percentage points. On a Unitree GO2, VLN-Flash improves navigation success and cuts the mean wait between actions by about 160 ms after subtracting network transmission time.

AI.tldr: 针对自回归视觉语言导航策略需逐动作等待依赖预测链的问题，VLN-Flash 提出免训练并行解码器：一次前向评估完整动作前缀树，并按分数边际自适应决定执行深度。作者报告在 Uni-NaVid 与 StreamVLN 上动作解码近 3× 加速，在 R2R-CE/RxR-CE 上成功率最高提升 2.7 个百分点，并在 Unitree GO2 上减少约 160 ms 的动作间平均等待。
AI.motivation: 自回归生成动作序列时，机器人必须等待一串相互依赖的预测，导致动作间延迟。摘要指出，小离散动作词表使并行评估短视界计划成为可能，这是方法成立的前提。
AI.method: 对原 VLN 策略，VLN-Flash 在单次前向中评估完整动作前缀树。它用分支特定注意力和匹配的 token 位置，在精确算术下保持原策略对每个前缀的条件动作分布。随后比较每一步贪心前缀与其最强替代项的分数边际，决定要执行多少动作；机器人执行所选深度下联合分数最高的计划，然后再重新观测。相对原生自回归逐动作解码，它改变的是解码与执行方式，不训练新策略。
AI.result: 作者报告：匹配输入下，Uni-NaVid 与 StreamVLN 上的动作解码相对原生自回归近 3× 加速；相比原生自回归解码器，R2R-CE 与 RxR-CE 上成功率与 SPL 提升，成功率增益最高 2.7 个百分点；在真实 Unitree GO2 上导航成功率提升，扣除网络传输时间后动作间平均等待减少约 160 ms。摘要未报告绝对成功率/SPL、统计显著性、具体硬件与完整实验条件。
AI.conclusion: 对具身导航，免训练并行解码加自适应执行可在不重训策略的前提下降低动作解码等待，并可能在匹配输入下保持原策略分布。作者报告的速度、精度与真机时延改善支持这一方向，但证据仅来自摘要，缺少绝对指标、显著性、算力开销与更广泛场景验证，不能外推为通用结论。

title: Sim-to-Real Room-Mediated Object-Goal Navigation with ROS 2 and Nav2
comment: 9 pages. Accepted to ACRA (Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation) 2026
summary: Although object-goal navigation (ObjectNav) approaches are usually evaluated in simulation, which offers scale and repeatable environments, real-world deployments are rarely examined beyond feasibility demonstrations. This paper presents the deployment of Room-Mediated Co-occurrence, an ObjectNav policy that reasons over Room Probability Vectors (RPVs), on two robotic platforms (Boston Dynamics Spot and Clearpath Robotics TurtleBot 4) through a robot-agnostic ROS 2 bridge. We study how these semantic priors generalise to physical environments and describe the adaptations required to transfer RPV from simulation to hardware, covering sensing, localisation, and the action interface. Across 66 trials on Spot, searching for 11 object categories from two starting positions in a university postgraduate research facility, RPV achieves a raw Success Rate (SR) of 0.455. Our analysis identifies undetected glass walls, entry into off-limits areas, limited usable depth range, target size, and mismatch between the room lexicon and physical layout as plausible contributors to the 8.4 percentage-point gap between the real-world SR and the reported simulated SR of 0.539. Code is available at this https URL .

title: AgenticJevNav: Agentic Object Search and Navigation via Event-Driven Verification
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Project page: this http URL
summary: Agentic navigation must maintain goals and adapt actions from incomplete evidence despite execution failures and delayed inference. We present AgenticJevNav, which links goal-directed planning, evidence memory, event-triggered verification, and bounded execution. The Agent plans from RGB, odometry, memory, and feedback, retaining goal ownership while authorizing a bounded action set. Jev reviews structured evidence after blocked/failed execution or two consecutive low-progress segments. Version, freshness, and once-only checks govern decision application. A single executor and independent RGB reflex constrain motion. Goal revisions revoke obsolete requests and actions before replanning. Across six simulated task families, AgenticJevNav achieves 73.33% SR over 60 trials, 21.67 percentage points above the next-best Agent-only aggregate control under differing historical protocols. A real-world GENISOM L1 quadruped deployment achieves 70.0% success over 30 trials, including bounded search reporting. Together, the simulation and physical-robot results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed architecture, while remaining failures highlight opportunities to improve grounding, approach planning, and runtime.

title: TMA: Sim-to-Real Forceful Humanoid Manipulation via Tactile-Driven Motor Adaptation
summary: Recent humanoid loco-manipulation in articulated environments has largely focused on geometry-dominant interactions, where success is primarily determined by geometric alignment and motion execution. In contrast, forceful multi-finger manipulation requires the robot to adapt to real-world uncertainties in contact and interaction dynamics. We present Tactile-Driven Motor Adaptation (TMA) and an integrated whole-body system for zero-shot sim-to-real forceful humanoid manipulation, and study round-doorknob opening as a challenging benchmark requiring stable multi-finger frictional grasping, sufficient torque generation without slip, force-regulated pushing, and whole-body stability. TMA structures policy learning around interactions observable through tactile feedback, uses cone geometry as an inductive bias for multi-finger contact representation, and adapts motor behavior online from tactile history. An upper-body manipulation policy is trained alongside a pretrained general locomotion controller to coordinate dexterous interaction and whole-body stabilization. Trained entirely in simulation, TMA transfers zero-shot to a Unitree G1 humanoid with BrainCo Revo2 multi-fingered hands and substantially outperforms standard Rapid Motor Adaptation (RMA) and reactive tactile policy baselines across four commercial round doorknobs in the real world.

AI.tldr: 针对 forceful 多指操作中真实接触与交互动力学不确定的问题，TMA 以触觉历史在线调整运动，并用锥几何作为多指接触表示的归纳偏置，配合预训练运动控制器构成全身系统。作者报告完全在仿真中训练后可零样本迁移到 Unitree G1 真机，在四个商用圆形门把手上大幅优于 RMA 与反应式触觉基线，但摘要未给出任何数值结果。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，现有 articulated environments 中的人形 loco-manipulation 多聚焦于几何对齐与运动执行；而 forceful 多指操作要求机器人适应真实世界接触与交互动力学中的不确定性。
AI.method: 输入是可通过触觉反馈观测到的交互历史。TMA 围绕这些交互组织策略学习，用锥几何作为多指接触表示的归纳偏置，并依据触觉历史在线调整运动行为。系统同时训练上肢操作策略与预训练通用运动控制器，以协调灵巧交互与全身稳定。输出是可在仿真中训练、零样本迁移到真机的 forceful 人形操作策略；与标准 RMA 和反应式触觉策略基线相比，核心变化是触觉驱动的在线运动适应与接触表示方式。

title: Recovery-Guided Model-Based Diffusion for Safety-Critical Legged Locomotion
summary: Safety-critical high-speed legged locomotion requires motion planners to balance safety foresight with online computational efficiency. Although short prediction horizons reduce rollout costs, they provide limited safety foresight, and strict safety constraints severely restrict the feasible trajectory space. We propose a recovery-guided model-based diffusion (MBD) framework for safety-critical legged locomotion. It incorporates a learned terminal recovery critic into short-horizon trajectory optimization. Specifically, the critic approximates the worst-case future clearance margin along rollouts of a designated recovery policy. We introduce a feasibility-guided refinement strategy that combines within-horizon constraints and terminal recoverability at each sampling stage, while retaining feasible elites to mitigate sampling-support loss. Across 50 paired randomized Unitree Go2 obstacle-avoidance trials, our approach achieves zero collisions and 98% strict-clearance success, while requiring substantially less computation than long-horizon MBD baselines. A project page is available at this https URL .

AI.tldr: 针对安全关键高速足式运动，作者把“终端可恢复性”学成一个 critic 并嵌入短时域扩散轨迹优化，在 50 次成对随机化 Unitree Go2 避障试验中报告 0 碰撞、98% 严格间隙成功率，且计算量明显少于长时域 MBD 基线。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，安全关键的高速足式运动要求运动规划同时兼顾安全预见性与在线计算效率；短预测时域虽降低 rollout 开销，却只能提供有限的安全预见，而严格安全约束又会大幅压缩可行轨迹空间。
AI.method: 输入是足式运动的轨迹优化问题：在短时域内采样并优化轨迹。方法新增两部分：一是学习一个“终端恢复 critic”，它估计在一条指定恢复策略的 rollout 上可能出现的最坏情况未来间隙余量（worst-case future clearance margin），把远期安全信息压缩成一个终端项；二是在每个采样阶段做可行性引导的细化，同时考虑时域内约束与终端可恢复性，并保留可行 elite 样本以缓解采样支撑集丢失。输出是满足约束、且被判定为终端可恢复的运动轨迹，交给足式机器人执行。相对所述基线（长时域 MBD），改动点是把长时域安全性换成短时域优化加恢复 critic。

title: ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models
summary: World-action models (WAMs) augment vision-language-action policies (VLAs) with future prediction so that the policy can anticipate how its actions will affect the physical world. Existing WAMs supervise complete future observations. However, observations typically change little over an action chunk, so the future loss is dominated by copying static background content rather than learning task-relevant robot and object motion, limiting policy learning. Moreover, existing WAMs rely on large video generation models or separate world models, incurring heavy training and inference compute that hinders closed-loop deployment. To improve policy performance, we propose visual residual learning, supervising only the feature change from the current frame to the future frame in a frozen DINOv3 space. Compared with complete future features, this residual learning target yields a higher feature rank with richer and more diverse representations of scene changes, and spatially concentrates on the robot arm and manipulated objects rather than the background. To further improve computational efficiency, we present ResWAM, a residual world-action model with 2.3B parameters in total, including a lightweight 0.5B dual-branch DiT that jointly trains an action branch and a residual branch via conditional flow matching. Without robot pretraining (i.e., pretraining on external robot action trajectories beyond the benchmark demonstrations), ResWAM achieves top average success rates on LIBERO-Plus (81.1%), RoboTwin 2.0 (93.8%), and RoboDojo (9.40% success, 13.41 score) at the lowest training (2.7-4.0 TFLOPs) and inference compute (1.0-1.4 TFLOPs), and leads real-robot Open, Put, and Stack (80.0% average, +10.0% over $\pi_{0.5}$) at 92.7 ms latency.

AI.tldr: 现有世界-动作模型（WAM）监督完整未来观测，损失被静态背景复制主导，且依赖大型视频生成模型或独立世界模型导致算力高。ResWAM 改为在冻结 DINOv3 空间中只监督"当前帧到未来帧"的特征残差，并用 2.3B 参数模型（含 0.5B 双分支 DiT）通过条件流匹配联合训练动作与残差分支。作者报告在无机器人预训练下取得 LIBERO-Plus 81.1%、RoboTwin 2.0 93.8% 等平均成功率，并在真实机器人 Open/Put/Stack 上达到 80.0% 平均成功率。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出两个具体缺口：一是观测在一个动作块内变化很小，监督完整未来观测会让未来损失被"复制静态背景"主导，学不到任务相关的机械臂与物体运动，从而限制策略学习；二是现有 WAM 依赖大型视频生成模型或独立世界模型，训练与推理算力沉重，妨碍闭环部署。
AI.method: 输入是当前帧（在冻结 DINOv3 特征空间中表示）。关键改动是监督目标：不再监督完整未来观测/未来特征，而是只监督当前帧到未来帧的特征变化，即"视觉残差"。模型侧，ResWAM 共 2.3B 参数，其中包含一个轻量 0.5B 双分支 DiT，通过条件流匹配联合训练一个动作分支和一个残差分支，因此同时产出动作与残差预测。相对摘要所述基线，它去掉了完整未来观测监督，也不再依赖大型视频生成模型或独立世界模型。
AI.result: 作者报告：在无机器人预训练（不使用基准演示之外的外部机器人动作轨迹预训练）条件下，ResWAM 在 LIBERO-Plus（81.1%）、RoboTwin 2.0（93.8%）、RoboDojo（9.40% success，13.41 score）取得"最高平均成功率"，训练算力 2.7-4.0 TFLOPs、推理算力 1.0-1.4 TFLOPs 为所报告的最低值。真实机器人 Open、Put、Stack 平均 80.0%，比 π_0.5 高 10.0%，延迟 92.7 ms；摘要未说明该 10.0% 是相对提升还是百分点差异。摘要未报告样本量、随机种子、显著性检验与消融。另有定性比较：残差监督目标相比完整未来特征具有更高特征秩、更丰富多样的场景变化表示，并空间上集中于机械臂与被操作物体而非背景，摘要未给出对应数值。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与世界模型研究的意义在于：世界-动作模型的监督信号可以从"重建完整未来观测"转向"只预测变化"，并以小型双分支结构替代大型视频生成/独立世界模型，从而在作者自报的算力区间内支撑闭环部署。证据边界：以上均为摘要中的作者自报结果，未经独立验证；真实机器人任务细节、统计可靠性与各组件贡献均未在摘要中给出，不能据此外推其泛化性或部署成熟度。

title: Towards Probabilistically Safe Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Deployment on Humanoid and Aerial Robots
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables robots to acquire complex skills, but standard RL formulations do not guarantee that learned policies satisfy safety constraints, which limits their use in safety-critical settings. Existing safe RL methods with provable guarantees typically support only restricted classes of constraints and require unbiased estimators of the objective and constraint functions, which prevents their direct integration with state-of-the-art algorithms such as proximal policy optimization (PPO). In this paper, we extend the recently introduced robust safe gradient flow-based reinforcement learning (RSGF-RL) framework to overcome these limitations. Our formulation accommodates a general class of trajectory-level safety constraints, including chance constraints such as collision avoidance with a prescribed probability, and our analysis allows for biased value and gradient estimators. We show that, with high probability, the constraint violation throughout training is bounded by the estimator bias plus a term that vanishes as the number of rollouts grows, and decays to this level if the initial policy is unsafe. We also establish the convergence properties of the iterates to approximate KKT points of the original safe RL problem. Finally, we show that RSGF-RL implemented with PPO-style estimates enables zero-shot sim-to-real deployment of whole-body control policies on a Unitree G1 humanoid and collision-free waypoint navigation on a Crazyflie drone.

title: DiffWAM: Learning World Action Model from Consecutive Visual Difference
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as an important paradigm in robot learning, jointly predicting future scene states and robot actions from current observations and instructions. However, future states entangle task-related changes with large amounts of task-irrelevant content, such as static backgrounds, which weakens the model's ability to capture changes relevant to task execution. To address this, we propose Difference World Action Model (DiffWAM), a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework that enhances world representations by jointly learning future-state prediction and consecutive visual difference prediction. We define consecutive visual differences as differences between the latent representations of consecutive observations, providing an explicit learning signal for temporal variation. The framework comprises a World Expert for future frame prediction, an Action Expert for action generation, and a Diff Expert for predicting these latent differences along the trajectory. A structured unidirectional attention mask conditions the Diff, World, and Action Experts solely on the current-frame representation while blocking attention between experts. This design allows both the World and Diff Experts to be removed during inference, introducing no additional inference overhead. DiffWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on the LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks and substantially improves over FastWAM on real-world manipulation tasks. Specifically, it attains average success rates of 98.8%, 92.65%, and 88.3%, outperforming the state-of-the-art baseline (i.e., FastWAM) by 1.75, 1.55, and 15.0 percentage points, respectively.

title: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
summary: Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our extrapolation method bridges the 10-Hz visual estimation with 50-Hz controller, enabling asynchronous visual processing and policy execution. Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning

summary: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

AI.tldr: JEPA4R 让世界模型直接以单深度相机点云为输入、在点云潜空间里预测与规划，并用手臂策略头在冻结潜表征上动作；作者报告 200 步内平均点误差在 1.1 cm 以内，MetaWorld 与 Adroit Relocate 分别达 98.4% 与 88.0%。

title: DAPPT: Domain-Aware Policies from Procedural Trajectories for Sim-to-Real Dexterous Tool Use
summary: Sim-to-real RL has achieved impressive results in dexterous manipulation but remains limited to tasks with accurate rigid-body simulation. However, these methods cannot be applied to skills that involve deformable and particles, with which the simulation speed will become too slow for large-scale RL learning. We present DAPPT, a sim-to-real framework for end-to-end dexterous tool-use manipulation skills, e.g., sand scooping, play-dough rod-rolling, without simulating non-rigid materials. Our method learns a domain-aware RL policy by tracking procedural trajectories parameterized by domain parameters, and distills it into an end-to-end domain-aware sensorimotor policy. Furthermore, explicit domain represen-tation enables fast selection of domain parameters that can maximize downstream task performance. We evaluate DAPPT end-to-end on six dexterous manipulation tasks, including sand scooping, play-dough rod-rolling, sand scraping, mouse-wheel scrolling, dispenser pressing, and spray triggering. Our method achieves 1.5-3.8x in task metrics through the best domain parameter and transfers zero-shot to the real world.

title: EgoSwarm: Learning Decentralized Robot Swarm Intelligence from Human Swarm Demonstrations
comment: 22 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Includes supplementary materials. Project page: this https URL
summary: Advancing from individual embodied intelligence to swarm embodied intelligence is a key step toward scalable, general-purpose embodied intelligence. Complex tasks often require multiple agents to divide responsibilities, coordinate handovers, and manipulate shared objects collaboratively. However, existing robot learning methods rely primarily on individual demonstrations, which provide limited supervision for modeling dependencies among agent actions, while collecting multi-robot demonstrations at scale remains difficult. Human egocentric demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, yet distributed observations from multiple participants cannot directly supervise decentralized policies. We introduce EgoSwarm, the first robot learning framework for learning decentralized multi-robot collaboration from human swarm demonstrations. EgoSwarm collects more than 50 hours of collaborative experience using a robot-free multi-person egocentric system. We introduce the Swarm Interaction Packet (SIP) and Swarm Interaction Token (SIT) to recover cross-agent interaction relations from distributed observations and transform this experience into local supervision consistent with deployment-time information constraints. We further propose SwarmVLA, which transfers knowledge of swarm behavior to decentralized policies conditioned on local observations, local history, and limited neighbor messages. SwarmVLA achieves a mean success rate of 72.2% across three categories of multi-robot collaborative tasks. Project page: this https URL .

AI.tldr: 为从人类群体示范中学习去中心化多机器人协作，EgoSwarm 用无机器人多人第一视角系统采集超过 50 小时协作经验，以 SIP/SIT 恢复跨智能体交互关系并生成局部监督，再训练 SwarmVLA 策略；作者报告 SwarmVLA 在三类多机器人协作任务上平均成功率 72.2%，但摘要未报告基线、仿真或真机条件。

title: PlanDiv: Test-Time Scaling with Latent Plans for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Test-time scaling improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies by drawing several action candidates and executing the best one. We find that its returns diminish quickly when the candidates are resampled from one decoder: they differ by noise rather than by plan, and for each of three resampling sources, going from four to eight candidates adds only 0.06-0.07 to the average number of completed tasks on CALVIN. We introduce PlanDiv, an action head that makes the candidates differ by plan: a lightweight planner proposes K latent plan hypotheses, a shared masked-diffusion executor decodes one action chunk per plan from a single backbone pass, and the policy executes the chunk that its own likelihood ranks highest. The plans are learned from demonstrations alone, without plan labels or rewards. With the backbone, data and training recipe held fixed, eight plan-conditioned candidates raise five-task chain success on CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D from 56.9% to 69.9%, while eight candidates from autoregressive, plan-free or same-plan resampling reach at most 64.9%. The same-plan baseline is PlanDiv's own checkpoint with the plan held fixed, so this gap comes from the plans, not from drawing more samples. On LIBERO-Long, four plans remove 40% of single-candidate failures, against at most 21% for matched resampling. On a real Franka arm the gain appears where a task admits more than one solution: PlanDiv is on par with a single-output OpenVLA-OFT+ baseline on a one-solution task and succeeds in 51 of 54 trials against 40 of 54 on two tasks with two solutions.

AI.tldr: VLA 的 test-time scaling 收益快速递减，因为同一解码器重采样的候选动作只是噪声不同、而非计划不同。PlanDiv 让轻量规划器提出多个潜在计划假设、由共享掩码扩散执行器在一次主干前向中为每个计划解码一段动作，并按策略自身似然择一执行；在主干、数据与训练配方固定的条件下，CALVIN ABC→D 五任务链成功率由 56.9% 升至 69.9%。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，从同一个解码器重采样多个动作候选时，收益会迅速衰减：候选之间是噪声差异而不是计划差异。作者报告，对三个重采样来源而言，候选数从 4 增加到 8，在 CALVIN 上只让平均完成任务数增加 0.06–0.07。
AI.method: 输入是演示数据（摘要明确说明不需要计划标签，也不需要奖励）。机制上，PlanDiv 是一个动作头：一个轻量规划器提出 K 个潜在计划假设；一个共享的 masked-diffusion 执行器在单次主干前向中为每个计划解码一个 action chunk；策略执行其自身似然排名最高的那个 chunk。相对基线的变化在于候选之间的差异来源——不再是同一解码器的重采样噪声，而是不同的潜在计划；摘要强调主干、数据与训练配方保持不变。
AI.result: 作者报告：8 个计划条件候选把 CALVIN ABC→D 五任务链成功率从 56.9% 提升到 69.9%，而自回归、无计划或同计划重采样的 8 个候选最高只到 64.9%；同计划基线是 PlanDiv 自身在计划固定下的检查点，作者据此认为差距来自计划而非采样数。LIBERO-Long 上，4 个计划消除了 40% 的单候选失败，匹配重采样最多为 21%。真机 Franka 上，收益出现在任务存在多解时：单解任务与单输出 OpenVLA-OFT+ 基线持平，双解的两个任务上 54 次试验成功 51 次，对比 40/54。此外，4→8 候选在 CALVIN 上仅带来 0.06–0.07 的平均完成任务数增量。以上均为作者报告，未经独立验证。
AI.conclusion: 该工作把 test-time scaling 的候选多样性从噪声层面移到计划层面，并且只用演示数据学习潜在计划，这对需要多解策略的 VLA 与以潜在计划为接口的世界模型方向提供了一个具体做法。证据边界：摘要只给出 CALVIN、LIBERO-Long 与一个 Franka 平台上的结果，作者自己也表明单解任务上并无增益，说明收益依赖任务是否允许多解；摘要未报告推理开销、计划器规模或统计显著性。

title: Stochastic Self-Distillation for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance in robotics through imitation learning, yet fine-tuning them with on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is limited. In group-based RL methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), every rollout step requires multi-step ODE integration, and the sampler's limited stochasticity leads to rollout groups with low variance. We propose VLA-SSD, which addresses both high inference latency and limited stochasticity. In particular, our method self-distills a pretrained flow-matching action head into a stochastic one-step policy by conditioning a single-jump generator on a Brownian path. We derive a conditional action density via our stochastic one-step policy, enabling efficient post-training via likelihood-ratio RL algorithms. We show that distilling VLA-SSD from the $\pi_0$ VLA reduces the action head's forward-pass time by a factor of 7.7, at the cost of a 5.5% relative decrease in the success rate on the LIBERO benchmark. However, by leveraging the increased sample diversity of VLA-SSD during group generation, post-training a $\pi_{0.5}$ VLA using GRPO yields a 20.6% relative improvement.

AI.motivation: 基于 flow 的 VLA 模型在模仿学习下表现强，但用 on-policy 强化学习微调受限：在 GRPO 这类 group-based RL 中，每次 rollout 的每一步都需要多步 ODE 积分，造成高推理延迟；同时采样器随机性有限，使 rollout group 内方差偏低。

title: Lift, See, Act: Hierarchical Robot Policy Pretraining with 3D Foundation Models
summary: Robot policy pretraining based on human videos is crucial for improving the policy's generalization ability. One main challenge for this task is the lack of explicit action-relevant representations in such unlabeled data. Recent works tend to estimate 3D hand motion trajectories from videos using 3D foundation models (3D FMs). However, they keep solely the sparse trajectories as supervision, ignoring the rich, fine-grained information produced during the trajectory extraction process. To address this issue, we propose LSA, a hierarchical robot policy pretraining framework that includes three phases: Lift, See, and Act. Specifically, the Lift phase elevates 2D video observations into dense 3D representations by adaptively aligning features in the policy's shallow layers with the intermediate representations extracted from multiple 3D FMs. Building upon these lifted representations, the See phase equips the policy with explicit geometric and interactive awareness through dual guidance. It introduces depth-map reconstruction to help the model comprehend 3D spatial layouts and utilizes hand region cues to explicitly supervise the encoder's attention toward task-relevant interaction hotspots. Empowered by the dense 3D representation learning and precise spatial guidance, our policy achieves robust and accurate robotic manipulation in the Act phase. Extensive experiments on diverse simulation and real-world tasks demonstrate that LSA significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches. title: SAFER: Navigating the Exploration-Exploitation Dilemma in World-Model-Based Planning for Autonomous Driving
summary: An autonomous vehicle must foresee the consequences of its actions, especially in the rare, time-critical situations where crashes happen. A world model offers this foresight, but only within the coverage of its training data, which poses an exploration-exploitation dilemma. Within this coverage a planner can hardly improve on the data, and beyond it the model's errors mislead it. Logs of competent driving rarely contain the failures that would widen the coverage, and agents that learn from interaction gain them only by failing themselves, without being shown what to do instead. We propose SAFER, a framework that learns offline from failures that others make, judged by an expert, and keeps learning online from its own driving. Offline, partially trained agents and scripted, recoverable perturbations Stage failures in simulation, and an expert Annotates every visited state with its action and value, so that much of what the planner explores is covered before it drives. In planning, a chunked latent world model Foresees the consequences fast enough for real-time use, and a risk-aware sampling-based planner Evaluates candidate maneuvers by their return minus a bounded collision penalty. Online, a loop continuously Refines the model wherever this driving leaves the coverage of the offline data. In closed-loop evaluation against the compared methods, SAFER reaches the highest route completion and reward per step on the CARLA Leaderboard routes, 0.95 and 0.77 from a privileged bird's-eye view, and the highest episode reward in MetaDrive, 53.4 in regular and 49.0 in safety-critical traffic. title: XMimic and XSoma: Learning Humanoid Motion Tracking and Locomotion in Under a Minute
summary: We present XMimic and XSoma, which learn humanoid motion tracking and locomotion on rough terrain in under a minute of training. Both follow SuperMimic, which learns a world model of the robot and optimizes the policy with analytic gradients through short rollouts imagined in this model. Existing implementations of this method do not make use of larger GPUs, as every training iteration is a long chain of small GPU operations that run one after another. XMimic and XSoma therefore shorten this chain and run the steps of every iteration at the same time on up to four GPUs. We compile the complete training loop with JAX, including the MuJoCo Warp simulator. For locomotion, XSoma leaves only the dynamics of the robot to the world model and computes everything else exactly, including the terrain height under the feet. It learns with a horizon of one second and without a critic. On four H100 GPUs, XMimic learns to track all 40 LAFAN1 clips with the Unitree G1 in 0.86 minutes, 3.7 times faster than BlinkMimic on one GPU. XSoma reaches the tracking target that Holosoma's tests set for FastSAC in 0.77 minutes, 12.3 times faster than FastSAC on one GPU, while needing only an eighth of its environment steps.

AI.tldr: XMimic 与 XSoma 沿用 SuperMimic 的“学机器人世界模型+短推演解析梯度”路线，把训练迭代中串行的小算子并行到最多四张 GPU 并用 JAX 编译整个训练循环，使人形动作跟踪与崎岖地形行走的训练时间降到一分钟以内。
AI.motivation: SuperMimic 类方法虽能学世界模型并用解析梯度优化策略，但现有实现每次训练迭代都是一长串依次执行的小型 GPU 算子，因此无法利用更大的 GPU 资源，训练速度受限。
AI.method: 输入是人形机器人（Unitree G1）与参考动作片段或崎岖地形；方法沿用 SuperMimic：先学一个机器人世界模型，再在其内部做短时想象推演，用解析梯度直接优化策略，输出可执行的动作跟踪/行走策略。相对既有实现的关键改动是缩短这条串行算子链，让每次迭代的各个步骤在最多四张 GPU 上同时运行，并用 JAX 编译包含 MuJoCo Warp 模拟器在内的完整训练循环。XSoma 进一步只把机器人自身动力学交给世界模型，其余量（含脚下地形高度）都精确计算，学习时用 1 秒的推演时域且不使用 critic。

AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与世界模型研究而言，该工作说明“世界模型 + 短推演解析梯度”这类策略学习的主要瓶颈可能来自算子串行与框架开销，而非算法本身：通过把迭代步骤并行到多 GPU 并全流程编译，可把人形动作跟踪与地形行走训练压到一分钟以内；XSoma 的“仅动力学建模、其余精确计算 + 1 秒时域 + 无 critic”则提示混合精确计算可减少环境步数依赖。但证据仅来自摘要：所有训练在 MuJoCo Warp 模拟器中进行，摘要未报告真机部署、绝对性能指标、统计显著性或多 GPU/单 GPU 成本归一化。

title: ReRead: Wrong Predictions, Useful Representations - Correcting Frozen Robot Policies by Re-reading Their Own Representations
summary: When a pretrained robot policy fails on challenging tasks, common remedies include retraining the backbone, adding an external visual encoder, or introducing a memory module. We argue that wrong predictions do not imply wrong representations: a policy can retain the required information yet fail to read it out as the correct action. To test this view, we propose ReRead: with the backbone frozen, a corrector re-reads the current and two previous caches to predict an action residual. The corrector sees no images, is trained solely on offline demonstrations from all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and adds only 4.17% latency. Ablations and interventions show that the correction relies on the backbone's own representations: none of four external visual encoders adds further gain, and swapping in past caches from other trajectories sharply increases action error. title: Right Goal, Wrong Body: Re-grounding Frozen VLAs under Actuation Shift
comment: Accepted at the SPAIS Workshop at CoRL 2026
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are capable of producing desired robotic behaviors in ideal settings. However, they often fail when the robot's actuation changes at deployment. For example, remounting, mechanical wear, or command latency changes can lead to failed tasks and unsafe behaviors. To address the inevitable actuation shift, we propose ReGround, an inference-time method that keeps the VLA frozen and re-grounds its intended motion. ReGround learns the deployed robot's dynamics from task-agnostic motor babbling, and then tracks the policy's intended motion while staying close to the policy's own plan. ReGround activates only upon detecting a shift, and needs no rewards, demonstrations, or retraining. We show via two VLAs, eight LIBERO tasks, and five shift settings that ReGround can restore near-oracle success, such as raising $\pi_{0.5}$'s success from 0.16 to 0.90 under 400 ms latency, while remaining safer than a linear-calibration baseline. title: Vision-Language Grounded Semantic Navigation for Autonomous Mobile Robots
summary: Language-guided navigation enables mobile robots to interpret natural language commands and navigate toward user-specified targets in unstructured environments. However, integrating open-vocabulary visual perception with classical robotics pipelines for mapping and navigation remains a challenging problem. In this work, we present a complete ROS2-based system that combines frontier-based exploration, open-vocabulary object detection using Grounding DINO, depth-based 3D localization, and semantic mapping to enable end-to-end vision-language grounded navigation in simulation. The system accepts natural language commands such as ``go to the yellow box,'' detects candidate objects from RGB images using text prompts, estimates their positions in the world frame, and generates navigation goals executed by the Nav2 stack. In a Gazebo-based indoor environment with a TurtleBot3 robot, the system autonomously explored the room, detected three of the five target objects, and successfully executed both natural language navigation commands tested, without task-specific training. The results indicate that open-vocabulary grounding models can be integrated into classical navigation pipelines, though performance is limited by detection uncertainty, depth-based localization error, and incomplete exploration coverage. These findings highlight both the feasibility and current limitations of deploying vision-language grounded navigation systems using lightweight, CPU-only architectures.

title: NF-VLA: A Normalizing-Flow Baseline for Vision-Language-Action Learning
summary: Autoregressive normalizing flows (NFs) provide a tractable density for learning and sampling continuous robot actions. We show that a single maximum-likelihood objective can train vision--language--action (VLA) policies competitive with leading methods on manipulation benchmarks. We present NF-VLA, which combines conditional autoregressive normalizing flows with score-based action refinement. Its deep--shallow architecture concentrates visual, language, and proprioceptive prefix conditioning in a high-capacity deep block, while unconditioned shallow blocks provide a shared invertible action transformation. The vision--language backbone and flow are jointly trained by exact maximum likelihood on Gaussian-smoothed action chunks. The same learned density supplies a single score-based correction at inference, refining generated actions to account for training-time smoothing without a separately trained denoiser. Trained on LIBERO from a pretrained vision--language backbone without robot pretraining, NF-VLA achieves 98.35\% success across the four standard suites and 72.6\% on LIBERO-Plus using the same checkpoint without further fine-tuning. Ablations show that deep-only prefix conditioning and score-based refinement both improve closed-loop success. Together, these results establish carefully structured autoregressive flows as a competitive approach to VLA control, with one learned density supporting policy training, action generation, and refinement.

title: DexFormer 2.0: Towards a Cross-Embodiment Foundation Policy for Dexterous Grasping
summary: Dexterous grasping policies are usually trained for one arm paired with one hand. Every new pairing then needs its own policy, and the number of policies grows with every arm and hand added. We ask whether a single policy can control many arm-hand combinations and transfer to pairings and hands it has never seen. This is hard because robots differ in the number, layout, and dynamics of their joints, so their observations and actions share no common interface. We present DexFormer 2.0, a single reinforcement learning policy for cross-embodiment dexterous grasping. It maps every robot to a canonical joint interface with validity masks, encodes each joint's morphology with attention biased by the kinematic tree, and uses a Transformer-XL memory to infer embodiment-dependent dynamics from recent interaction. Trained on 18 combinations of four arms and six hands, it reaches 89% stable success on seen combinations and 51% on six held-out arm-hand pairs, outperforming GRU and DexFormer 1.0 baselines. Without fine-tuning, it also grasps with four new hand types and, through retargeting, with parallel grippers. Ablations show that memory, the kinematic-tree bias, and broader pairing coverage each matter for transfer. On a physical Flexiv arm, distilled students transfer zero-shot from simulation with two hands, including a held-out pair. Project website: this https URL .

title: TaF-Foundation: Wrench-Grounded Cross-Sensor Tactile Representations
summary: Tactile sensing is essential for contact-rich manipulation, yet heterogeneous sensing mechanisms and observation formats hinder cross-hardware transfer. Since physical contact is governed by Newtonian mechanics, we ground tactile representations in six-dimensional wrenches, establishing a common physical reference across sensing mechanisms. Specifically, we pair tactile observations from all sensors with wrench measurements, enabling shared physical supervision without requiring direct tactile-to-tactile pairing between sensors. To support learning at scale, we develop a dedicated acquisition platform and collect over 100 million paired tactile observations and wrench measurements from 24 sensors spanning four families of sensing principles. Building on this dataset, our framework combines sensor-specific input adaptation with a shared tactile encoder. By learning to reconstruct wrenches, the encoder maps observations from different sensors into a shared, continuous feature space grounded in contact physics. To leverage these representations for manipulation, we introduce TaF-Policy, which integrates tactile features with visual observations and robot states to generate action chunks. We evaluate the learned representations through wrench estimation, cross-sensor retrieval, few-shot adaptation to unseen sensors, and robotic manipulation. On the core benchmark, our method reduces single-frame force RMSE by 17.1% and improves cross-sensor retrieval R@1 by 13.11 percentage points over the strongest baseline. In manipulation experiments, TaF-Policy achieves average success rates of 51.33% across three simulated tasks and 46.25% across four real-world tasks, compared with 47.33% and 23.75%, respectively, for the strongest baselines evaluated on the same task sets. AI.method: 输入是来自不同触觉传感器的触觉观测，以及与之配对的力旋量测量（每个传感器都同时提供触觉观测与力旋量，无需传感器之间的直接触觉-触觉配对）。方法上，作者搭建了专用采集平台，收集 24 个传感器、覆盖四类传感原理的超过 1 亿对触觉观测与力旋量测量；框架由"传感器专属输入适配 + 共享触觉编码器"组成，编码器通过重构力旋量这一学习目标，把不同传感器的观测映射到以接触物理为基准的共享连续特征空间。在此基础上提出 TaF-Policy，将触觉特征与视觉观测、机器人状态融合，输出动作块（action chunks）。相对基线的改变在于：不再依赖触觉-触觉配对，而是用统一的力旋量监督实现跨传感器共享表征。

title: AsymEEF: Bimanual Manipulation with Asymmetric End Effectors
summary: Teleoperated demonstrations are costly to collect and rarely reusable across end-effectors with different kinematics and action spaces. This burden grows in bimanual manipulation, where each end-effector pair may require new data. We present AsymEEF, a framework for executable cross-end-effector demonstration generation and unified bimanual policy learning. Given a small source dataset, AsymEEF transfers demonstrations to heterogeneous combinations of two-, three-, and five-fingered end-effectors without additional teleoperation. Kinematic teacher anchors provide geometric supervision, while sparse real-world X-Calib anchors correct discrepancies in grasp execution. A shared encoder maps wrist poses and actuator states to a morphology-agnostic latent space, and a morphology-conditioned decoder reconstructs target commands. Generated trajectories undergo replay filtering for task-level executability. The representation also supports a unified bimanual visuomotor policy trained across multiple pairs. Across four simulated and six real-world tasks, AsymEEF improves replay success over adapted transfer baselines, achieves a mean replay-valid expansion gain of 16.6 times in simulation, and is evaluated through downstream policy training on real robots. title: FlowRow: Learning Navigation Behaviors in Agricultural Environments with Long-Horizon Goal-Conditioned Flow Matching Policies
summary: Autonomous monitoring and intervention in semi-structured agricultural environments, such as orchards and vineyards, require mobile robots to navigate to locations across diverse field configurations. This entails performing navigation behaviors including in-row driving, row turning and skipping, and inter-row traversal. Recent learning-based approaches have enabled robust in-row navigation from onboard perception, but navigation across rows typically requires a priori knowledge of field geometry to specify and tune row-transition maneuvers, preventing arbitrary transitions between rows. We address this challenge by framing navigation in these environments as a goal-directed navigation task, where a long-horizon goal is expressed relative to the robot and a planner generates local paths based on the goal and the robot's perceptual observations. We present FlowRow, a flow-matching-based local planner which models the distribution of diverse agricultural navigation behaviors as $\mathrm{SE}(2)$ paths using the long-horizon goal and depth perception. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce RowNavBench, a navigation benchmark for semi-structured agricultural environments developed in Isaac Sim, comprising 900 episodes across grape vineyards, lemon orchards, and apple orchards with varying row lengths, row and plant spacings, plant positions, and weed growth. FlowRow achieves 87% success, compared to 44% for the strongest generative behavior cloning baseline retrained on the same demonstrations. We will release our benchmark, data, and code upon acceptance.

title: ACiT: Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers
summary: Visuomotor policies condition action prediction on visual and proprioceptive observations. While historical proprioceptive sequences carry rich dynamic priors, current methods treat them as equal to high-dimensional vision, causing the proprioceptive signal to be overwhelmed. To identify what is lost in equal-conditioning fusion, we analyze proprioceptive data and find that strong inter-joint coupling is the key action-determining structure. This finding aligns with the neural sensorimotor loop, in which proprioception first forms a body-centered prior and vision is later calibrated via parietal remapping. Inspired by this, we propose ACiT, Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers, which reinforces historical joint-coupling as the primary condition with vision as a later calibration. This design is instantiated through three modules: Inverted State Encoding builds a proprioceptive prior via per-joint tokens and inter-joint self-attention. State-Visual Grounding lets joint tokens query visual evidence, making vision goal- and calibration-only. Inverted Action Chunking decodes per-joint trajectories independently. ACiT improves success rates on most LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world tasks, with the largest gains on those that require dynamics and coordination. The same conditioning design transferred to the VLA backbone pi_0-ACiT yields significant gains with better execution efficiency.

title: Learning and Verifying Progress: Closed-Loop Agentic Planning with Progress-Enhanced Execution for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Navigation
summary: Long-horizon vision-language navigation (VLN) requires agents to track instruction progress and recover from local errors before they propagate across subtasks. However, executors trained on expert trajectories encounter policy-induced state shifts during deployment, and their stop signals do not reliably indicate subtask completion. We introduce Learning and Verifying Progress for VLN (LeaP-VLN), an agentic VLN system that couples progress-aware execution with independent progress verification through plan--execute--verify--recover cycles. LeaP-VLN leverages progress both explicitly, through a progress verifier that verifies subtask completion before the agent advances and triggers dual-phase recovery upon route deviation, and implicitly, by co-training the executor on progress reasoning and action prediction to enhance the executor's progress awareness and corrective control. To adapt the executor to this closed-loop interface, we propose a two-stage progress-enhanced curriculum: behavior cloning on expert demonstrations, followed by joint training on demonstrations, expert action corrections, and progress-reasoning supervision. Policy-generated trajectories expose the executor to both intra-subtask drift and inter-subtask state shifts, aligning training with the deviations encountered during closed-loop execution. Extensive experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE demonstrate state-of-the-art success rates among monocular methods trained without additional navigation datasets, while real-world experiments further validate the effectiveness of LeaP-VLN in long-horizon navigation.

AI.tldr: 针对长时程 VLN 中执行器部署时出现"策略引发的状态偏移"、停止信号无法可靠指示子任务完成的问题，LeaP-VLN 把进度验证与进度感知执行器耦合进"规划—执行—验证—恢复"闭环，并用两阶段课程训练执行器；作者声明在 R2R-CE 与 RxR-CE 上取得（单目、未额外使用导航数据集训练的方法中）最优成功率，摘要未报告数值。

title: WiTac: Wrist-Informed Tactile Representations for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: Similar tactile contacts can call for different corrections depending on the configuration of the hand, object and target. Rather than supplying touch and wrist vision separately, fusing them before policy injection better grounds tactile features in visual context, yielding more accurate contact representations. We introduce Wrist-Informed Tactile Representations (WiTac), a pretrained encoder that learns such representations before action generation. Pretrained on nearly 300 hours of SharpaDex data, WiTac deeply fuses tactile signals with hand motion and wrist views into a comprehensive contact representation. Conditioning downstream VLA policies (GR00T N1.7 and $\pi_{0.5}$) on WiTac substantially improves task success over vision-only base policies across four contact-rich manipulation tasks (+28.8% and +15.0% on average), and further outperforms a wrist-free tactile encoder by 18.8% and 7.5%, respectively. title: Multi-CONDOR: Learning Multistable Motion Primitives from Demonstration
summary: Dynamical-system-based motion policies provide a framework for learning reactive robot motions with stability and convergence properties. Many manipulation tasks, however, admit several distinct goals or a continuous set of acceptable outcomes, requiring motion primitives that preserve these alternatives. Accommodating both goal structures within a unified framework with continuous, autonomous dynamics remains an open challenge. We propose a CONDOR-based framework, multi-CONDOR, for learning motion primitives with either multiple discrete attractors or a continuous attracting goal contour. The approach combines imitation learning with losses that encourage agreement between the learned task dynamics and latent reference systems encoding the desired attraction structure. We provide a Lyapunov-based analysis of the convergence properties of the learned motion dynamics. We evaluate the framework on simulated benchmarks with discrete goals, qualitative examples with continuous goal contours, and robotic grasping experiments. In simulation, multi-CONDOR reduces trajectory RMSE by approximately 72% compared with separately learned single-goal motion primitives selected by a state machine. For tasks with two and three goals, respectively, it reduces the fraction of evaluated initial states ending outside the goal tolerance from StableNODE's 0.31% and 7.29% to 0% in both settings. Experiments with a Franka Emika robot arm demonstrate successful grasping of a container by either of its two handles using motions learned from demonstrations. Together, these results show multi-CONDOR combines motion reproduction with the flexibility to converge to alternative valid outcomes.

AI.tldr: 许多操作任务存在多个离散目标或连续可接受结果，但已有的基于动力系统的运动策略难以在统一框架内保留这些替代目标。multi-CONDOR 以 CONDOR 为基础，用模仿学习加上“与编码期望吸引结构的潜在参考系统一致”的损失来学习多吸引结构运动基元；仿真中轨迹 RMSE 相比由状态机选择的单独单目标基元下降约 72%，Franka 机械臂上演示学习后可抓住容器两个把手之一。

title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
comment: 31 pages: 8-page main paper, references, and supplementary material. Project page: this https URL
summary: Frontier multimodal models can now control robots zero-shot from images, yet many manipulation tasks depend on contact forces that images cannot show. Bringing force to an API-only frozen model raises two challenges. First, contact evolves much faster than an API model can decide, so the system must close the loop on force beneath the model. Second, a frozen model cannot interpret raw force streams, so force must be returned in a form the model can reason about. Therefore, we present ForceHarness, a harness that lets frozen models use force without demonstrations or finetuning. After calibrating hand force from a wrist sensor or joint torques alone, ForceHarness addresses the first challenge with self-terminating force primitives that regulate force on their own and return at a contact event. To address the second challenge, a physics translation layer turns each force trace into physical quantities with uncertainty as the tool result. To evaluate ForceHarness against expert force controllers and learned policies under identical conditions, we also build HiddenPhys, a seven-task MuJoCo benchmark with hidden physical variables. On a real arm without a wrist force sensor, ForceHarness raises the zero-shot success rate of GPT-6 Astra from 3.3% to 90.0%. In simulation, it adds 17.5 percentage points on the public ForceBench suite and 34.3 percentage points on HiddenPhys, surpassing force-aware policies trained on demonstrations on both benchmarks and matching hand-written expert controllers on HiddenPhys. Ablations further show that smaller models make significantly better decisions when given physical quantities rather than raw force values.

title: Driving the Style: Velocity-Conditioned Whole-Body Control from Motion Demonstrations
summary: Achieving human-like behavior on humanoid robots has advanced rapidly by leveraging motion-capture demonstrations rather than hand-crafted cost functions. Adversarial imitation supplies a style signal that lets a policy fulfill a task while adhering to a desired style, but is difficult to transfer to hardware. Whole-body tracking through reinforcement learning instead deploys reliably and imitates demonstrations faithfully, but the resulting policies are conditioned on the future reference, so they require a reference trajectory at runtime and can fail when the motion differs from the training data. We train a humanoid policy directly with whole-body tracking rewards while restricting its actor to compact locomotion commands and robot observations. Reference motion supervises the reward and privileged critic, without supplying reference joint trajectories to the actor or requiring teacher distillation. The demonstrated style is thereby encoded in the policy through the tracking reward, so the robot reproduces the whole-body style under commanded velocities. Trained on a single random-walk motion and commanded with velocity profiles from held-out motions, our policy reaches at least 98\% success in simulation and completes every trial on the Unitree G1. On held-out slow walking, whole-body tracking drops to 2\% success and command-conditioned distillation to 56\%, and both fail on the real robot. On the trained motions, the joint position error of our policy stays within 8\% of whole-body tracking, and it has a higher style coverage than adversarial motion priors (AMP), which fell on the real robot without a safety crane.

title: Robotic Reward Models in the Foundation-Model Era
summary: Robotic reward models (RRMs) use foundation models to replace per-task reward engineering with reusable, task-conditioned evaluation. Yet under one name, their outputs answer different questions, from whether a task succeeded to which execution is better. This survey organizes 114 methods into five semantic families by the question their native outputs answer: Outcome, Absolute Progress, Relative, Temporal Value, and Hybrid. Within this taxonomy, we review how model design determines what an evaluator can judge, how raw experience becomes supervision, and how existing evaluation practice tests the result. The review exposes a gap: agreement with demonstration order and downstream policy gains do not show whether a reward tracks task fulfillment. We therefore introduce RRM-Bench-1K, 1,117 real-robot videos of closed-loop executions with task-state and camera-evidence labels, and four contrast suites that separate the credited condition from its usual cues. A unified study of 27 evaluators shows that the strongest final scores rank whole executions well enough for selection and filtering. Dense credit, however, follows the progression of an execution more closely than its task state, and no evaluator signals when the decisive view is missing. How much fidelity a reward model needs therefore depends on the decision it drives. We outline directions from real-failure supervision to metrics that separate task state from chronology, and open-source RRM-Hub, a toolbox in which 14 existing RRMs can be readily applied and new evaluators tested on the same capabilities.

AI.tldr: 这篇综述把 114 个机器人奖励模型（RRM）按"原生输出回答什么问题"归为五类语义家族，并发布 1,117 段真实机器人视频的 RRM-Bench-1K。统一评测 27 个评估器后作者指出：最强的最终分数适合排序整条执行，但密集信用更贴近执行的时间进程而非任务状态。
AI.motivation: 基础模型被用来替代逐任务奖励工程，但"机器人奖励模型"这一名称下，输出实际回答的是不同问题——从任务是否成功，到哪种执行更好。这种语义混淆使既有评测无法说明奖励是否真的跟踪任务完成度。
AI.method: 综述按评估器原生输出的语义把 114 个方法分为五类：Outcome（结果）、Absolute Progress（绝对进度）、Relative（相对）、Temporal Value（时间价值）、Hybrid（混合）。综述同时梳理三条线索：模型设计决定评估器能判断什么、原始经验如何转成监督信号、现有评测实践如何检验结果。为补上评测缺口，作者构建 RRM-Bench-1K：1,117 段真实机器人闭环执行视频，带任务状态与相机证据标注，并设计四组对比套件，把被评定的条件与其常见的伴随线索分离。产出还包括开源工具箱 RRM-Hub，可即用 14 个已有 RRM 并在同一能力上测试新评估器。
AI.result: 作者报告：在 27 个评估器的统一研究中，最强最终分数对整条执行的排序足以用于选择与过滤；但密集信用更贴合执行的时间进程而非任务状态，且没有任何评估器在决定性视角缺失时发出信号。摘要未报告任何数值指标、百分比改善或统计显著性。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的启示是：奖励模型的保真度需求取决于它驱动的决策，而非越高越好；把"任务状态"与"时间顺序"混为一谈的指标会误导选型。证据边界限于摘要：该结论来自 1,117 段真实机器人视频上的离线统一评测，摘要未报告真实闭环部署、计算开销或与具体策略训练收益的量化对比。

title: Cooperative Mobile Manipulation using Learned Dynamical Systems
summary: Cooperative mobile manipulation requires robots to coordinate their motions while ensuring whole-body collision avoidance and preserving task-relevant behaviors. We propose CALDS (Cooperative Adaptation of Learned Dynamical Systems), a framework that enables mobile manipulators to adapt learned single-agent behaviors for coordinated execution. Building on individual dynamical systems (DSs) learned from demonstrations, CALDS enables cooperative adaptation through two key components: Cooperative Policy Selection, which identifies compatible combinations of learned policies, and Temporal Adaptation, which ensures collision-free cooperation while preserving the spatial structure and convergence properties of the original behaviors. We evaluate CALDS across three diverse scenarios: assistive dressing, restaurant cleaning and serving, and drawer opening and object placement. Quantitative results demonstrate its effectiveness in improving task success and enabling safe, coordinated simultaneous execution while maintaining fidelity to demonstrated behaviors.

title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
summary: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

AI.tldr: 多数视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略仍只用较小的 VLM 主干，前沿规模表征的潜力未被利用。ScaleVLA 把 552B 的 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 主干接到可训练的动作 DiT 上，并在统一训练设定下比较 2B 至 552B 的主干，作者报告其在样本效率、LIBERO-PRO 泛化与真机插充电器任务上均优于较小主干。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，GPT-6 Astra 等前沿 VLM 已展现机器人控制能力，暗示大规模预训练能提供对物理动作有用的知识；但大多数 VLA 策略仍依赖小得多的 VLM 主干，这部分潜力基本未被开发。作者由此追问：前沿规模的表征能否为机器人学习提供更强的基础。摘要未报告此前方法在样本效率、泛化或精细操作上的具体失败数值。
AI.method: 输入为机器人学习任务中的视觉-语言观测与演示数据。方法把 552B 的 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 主干与一个可训练的动作 DiT 相连，由动作 DiT 输出动作（按摘要，以动作块 action chunk 为单位）。相对基线，核心改变是主干规模：在共享训练设定下系统比较 2B 至 552B 的 VLM，并围绕三项能力——样本效率、泛化、精细操作——做评估。摘要未说明主干是否冻结、动作 DiT 结构、训练数据或预训练细节。

title: Lazy-MOSAIC: Accelerating Skill-Centric Manipulation Planning with Learned Skill-Effect World Models
summary: Long-horizon manipulation tasks require a robot to perform a sequence of physical interactions with its environment, typically combining several different skills. Planning such behaviors efficiently is challenging: given a library of parameterized skills, solutions lie in a vast hybrid space of skill sequences and their parameters, and evaluating each candidate skill's feasibility and effect with a high-fidelity world model such as a physics simulator is computationally expensive. MOSAIC, a recent skill-centric approach, lets the skills guide a non-sequential search toward the regions of this space where they are likely to succeed; however, it pays the full cost of simulation for every parameterized skill it considers. In this work, we introduce Lazy-MOSAIC, a lazy planning framework that instead searches over hypothesized skill outcomes. A cheap learned skill-effect world model predicts, in a fraction of a millisecond, a skill's feasibility and the world state it produces. Lazy-MOSAIC then uses these predictions to focus expensive simulation on promising candidate skills and, when a hypothesis is invalidated, repairs only the affected part of the search, while ensuring that every skill in a returned plan is validated in simulation. We evaluate Lazy-MOSAIC on cluttered-shelf retrieval tasks of increasing difficulty and demonstrate it on a physical robot, showing that it plans substantially faster than baselines with fewer simulator queries, while matching or exceeding their success rate in every setting. AI.tldr: Lazy-MOSAIC 用「学到的技能效果世界模型」先预测每个参数化技能的可行性与结果状态，把昂贵仿真只花在有希望的候选上，并在假设被推翻时局部修复搜索。作者报告在杂乱货架取物任务上规划显著更快、仿真查询更少，且成功率在每类设定上持平或更高，但摘要未给出任何数值。

AI.method: 输入是参数化技能库与一个廉价的学习技能效果世界模型（skill-effect world model）。方法不再直接对技能参数做仿真评估，而是先对「假设的技能结果」做惰性（lazy）搜索：世界模型以不到一毫秒的时间预测某技能的可行性和它将产生的世界状态；这些预测被用来把昂贵的仿真集中到有希望的候选技能上；当某个假设被仿真推翻时，只修复搜索中受影响的那部分，而不是重做全局搜索。输出是一条技能序列及其参数构成的计划，且该计划中的每个技能都在仿真中被验证过。相对 MOSAIC 的关键改变是：仿真不再是每个候选技能的必经评估步骤，而由学习模型的预测来筛选对象与时机。

title: The Sense Paradigm for World Models
summary: Latent world models predict the future in an embedding space rather than in pixels. An encoder trained only to predict collapses and maps every observation to the same point, so existing models add a mechanism against collapse, such as a target network, a variance penalty or a distribution penalty. These mechanisms keep the embedding from collapsing, but they leave its distances without meaning, and the model cannot tell a reversible transition from an irreversible one. We propose Sense, a single cross-entropy loss over the directed distance $d(x\to y)=\sum_i \mathrm{ReLU}(y_i-x_i)$ that replaces these mechanisms. The loss avoids collapse on its own, and since the encoder no longer needs the predictor, the predictor is fitted afterwards to fixed embeddings by plain regression. On four pixel environments, the return distance learned by Sense detects irreversible transitions with an AUC between 0.95 and 1.00, where LeWorldModel stays between 0.39 and 0.59. On TwoRoom, the navigation benchmark of LeWorldModel, planning with Sense reaches the goal in 100% of episodes against 91% for LeWorldModel. As the goal moves farther away, the planning failure rate of every baseline grows, while that of Sense stays near zero in Cup, Cliff and Sokoban and is the lowest of all methods in Pendulum.

AI.tldr: 针对隐空间世界模型编码器易塌缩、而现有反塌缩机制又让嵌入距离失去语义的问题，Sense 用单个作用于有向距离 d(x→y)=Σ ReLU(y_i−x_i) 的交叉熵损失替代目标网络/方差/分布惩罚，并让预测器在固定嵌入上事后回归。作者报告四个像素环境的不逆转变检测 AUC 为 0.95–1.00（LeWorldModel 0.39–0.59），TwoRoom 规划成功率 100%（LeWorldModel 91%）。
AI.motivation: 仅以预测为目标的编码器会塌缩，把每个观测映射到同一点；现有模型靠目标网络、方差惩罚或分布惩罚阻止塌缩，但这些机制只保住嵌入不塌缩，没有赋予其距离语义，模型因而无法区分可逆与不可逆的转变。
AI.method: 输入是观测（像素环境中的画面），经编码器得到嵌入，训练信号不是让编码器去迎合预测器，而是对嵌入对有向距离 d(x→y)=Σ_i ReLU(y_i−x_i) 施加单一交叉熵损失。相对基线（使用目标网络/方差惩罚/分布惩罚的世界模型），该损失本身就足以避免塌缩，因而编码器不再需要预测器配合；预测器随后在固定嵌入上用普通回归单独拟合。输出是距离有语义、可区分可逆与不可逆转变的嵌入，以及在该嵌入上回归得到的预测器，可继续用于规划。

title: ARMFUL: Learning Whole-Arm Grasp Configurations for Single-Arm Pickup of Large Objects
summary: Many everyday objects, such as storage boxes, baskets, and chairs, are too large or heavy for a gripper to grasp, yet a single arm can still pick them up by wrapping around and supporting them. Such grasps are hard to learn: wrapping motions are difficult to teleoperate, and existing datasets contain little whole-arm pickup data. We introduce WAG (Whole-Arm Grasp Dataset), the first large-scale dataset for single-arm pickup of large objects, with 1.7~million joint configurations across 793 objects. We sample configurations directly in joint space, execute each through squeeze and lift primitives in simulation, and stress-test survivors under active shaking and external forces. To demonstrate the utility of WAG and accomplish the whole-arm pickup task, we develop ARMFUL, a whole-arm pickup pipeline that pairs a diffusion model trained on WAG, generating whole-arm grasps from the object's point cloud, with a motion planner that reaches them collision-free before the same squeeze-and-lift execution. In simulation, ARMFUL reaches 85.4\% lift success on training and 69.9\% on held-out objects, and it lifts the object in 70 of 100 trials on a physical Franka arm across 10 IKEA objects.

AI.tldr: 针对大型物体难以用夹爪抓取、缠绕动作难遥操作且数据稀缺的问题，作者构建 WAG 数据集并训练扩散模型生成全身臂抓取配置，再由无碰撞运动规划器执行挤压-抬升。仿真中报告 85.4% 训练物体与 69.9% 留出物体提升成功率，物理 Franka 上 10 个 IKEA 物体 100 次试验成功 70 次。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出：许多日常物体（收纳箱、篮子、椅子）太大或太重，夹爪无法抓取；单臂可环抱支撑拾取，但这类抓取难学，因为缠绕动作难以遥操作，且现有数据集很少包含全身臂拾取数据。
AI.method: 输入是物体的点云；ARMFUL 使用在 WAG 上训练的扩散模型生成全身臂抓取（关节配置），再由运动规划器无碰撞地到达该配置，最后执行与数据构建相同的 squeeze-and-lift 原语。WAG 通过直接在关节空间采样配置、在仿真中执行挤压与抬升，并对存活配置施加主动摇晃和外部力压力测试来构建。
AI.result: 作者报告：仿真中 ARMFUL 的 lift success 为 training 85.4%、held-out objects 69.9%；物理 Franka 臂上，10 个 IKEA 物体共 100 次试验中成功提起 70 次。摘要未报告与任何基线的数值对比、相对提升或统计显著性；85.4% 与 69.9% 是绝对成功率，不是相对提升。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能而言，该工作把全身臂抓取数据生成、扩散式抓取配置生成与无碰撞运动规划串成单臂拾取大型物体的流程；仿真压力测试和真实 Franka 试验提供了初步证据，但证据限于摘要报告的设置，且无基线对比，不能推断对其他机器人、物体或真实场景的泛化。本文未提出显式世界模型。
